title: Void Ending in a Square to Saturn
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3, Book III chapter 1 and Book III chapter 8

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The square is one of the two worst aspects in the lunar doctrine, an enmity the text grades as moderate because the signs it joins stand two natures apart. The counsel that guards every election runs exactly here: watch the square and the opposition in everything, and keep the Moon from the unfortunate planets in these figures above all.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a square to Saturn, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his weight and his cold. Saturn holds the power of retention, and when he is afflicted he is the gravest of the impediments: the science of law and profound knowledge, deep and occult properties, the building trades, and working the soil are his, with murky rivers, black mountains, deep wells, and desert places among his locations. Lead and iron are his metals, black his color, the bitter taste his own. Well disposed and direct, he gives purity, long life, standing, honor, riches, and durable inheritances; afflicted, he is the lord of poverty, misery, pain, and imprisonment.
